concrete_changes.before: This is not personality typing. This is a rule set. And rule sets, when applied iteratively across a grid of states, produce cellular automata.
concrete_changes.after: I want to read that relationship table as material for a rule set. To make it an automaton, I still have to specify states, neighbourhoods and an update rule.
concrete_changes.reason: Replace performed equivalence with actual modelling burden.

concrete_changes.before: These values are not arbitrary. They represent the strength of constructive interference between planetary fields.
concrete_changes.after: The values encode the categories in this proposed model. They are not measurements of interference between planetary fields.
concrete_changes.reason: Separate chosen weights from unsupported empirical strength.

concrete_changes.before: Mercury befriends everyone except the Moon.
concrete_changes.after: In the displayed Mercury row, Sun, Mercury and Venus have weight5; the other entries, including Moon, have weight4.

concrete_changes.before: The Graha friendship matrix exhibits identical behavior. Nine planets. Three relationship types. A fixed rule set.
concrete_changes.after: The proposed Graha model starts with nine planets, three relationship types and a fixed table. Whether its update rules produce interesting behaviour has to be demonstrated.
concrete_changes.reason: Remove unproven identical-behaviour and fragment triad.

concrete_changes.before: No two charts produce identical automata evolution, yet all charts follow the same fundamental rules.
concrete_changes.after: Different initial charts could be compared under the same specified rules; their evolution is a result to compute, not assume.

concrete_changes.before: The automaton's rules predict instability before it manifests.
concrete_changes.after: A working implementation would let us examine instability inside the model. It would not, by itself, predict upheaval in a life.

concrete_changes.before: The language is different. The mathematics is the same.
concrete_changes.after: The comparison is useful if it makes the rule choices visible. A shared vocabulary of patterns is only the beginning of that work.
